375: func smokeCoverageMapping(d smokeDiscovery, sprint string) *SmokeCoverageMapping {
376: 	for _, mapping := range d.SprintMappings {
377: 		if mapping.Sprint != sprint {
378: 			continue
379: 		}
380: 		suites := map[string]bool{}
381: 		for _, suite := range mapping.Suites {
382: 			suites[suite] = true
383: 		}
384: 		out := &SmokeCoverageMapping{
385: 			Sprint:           mapping.Sprint,
386: 			Suites:           append([]string(nil), mapping.Suites...),
387: 			Complete:         mapping.Complete,
388: 			NotApplicable:    mapping.NotApplicable,
389: 			Rationale:        mapping.Rationale,
390: 			RequiredCoverage: append([]string(nil), mapping.RequiredCoverage...),
391: 			Tests:            []SmokeCoverageTest{},
392: 		}
393: 		for _, test := range d.Tests {
394: 			if suites[test.Suite] {
395: 				out.Tests = append(out.Tests, SmokeCoverageTest{ID: test.ID, Suite: test.Suite, Coverage: append([]string(nil), test.Coverage...)})
396: 			}
397: 		}
398: 		sort.Strings(out.Suites)
399: 		sort.Slice(out.Tests, func(i, j int) bool { return out.Tests[i].ID < out.Tests[j].ID })
400: 		return out
401: 	}
402: 	return nil
403: }

405: func populateSmokeCoverageRequirements(mapping *SmokeCoverageMapping, requirementsPath string) {
406: 	if mapping == nil {
407: 		return
408: 	}
409: 	descriptions := map[string]string{}
410: 	if content, err := os.ReadFile(requirementsPath); err == nil {
411: 		inAcceptance := false
412: 		index := 0
413: 		for _, line := range strings.Split(string(content), "\n") {
414: 			trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
415: 			if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "## ") {
416: 				inAcceptance = strings.EqualFold(strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(trimmed, "## ")), "Acceptance Criteria")
417: 				continue
418: 			}
419: 			if !inAcceptance || (!strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "- [ ] ") && !strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "- [x] ") && !strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "- [X] ")) {
420: 				continue
421: 			}
422: 			index++
423: 			descriptions[fmt.Sprintf("AC-%02d", index)] = strings.TrimSpace(trimmed[6:])
424: 		}
425: 	}
426: 	mapped := map[string][]string{}
427: 	for _, test := range mapping.Tests {
428: 		for _, coverageID := range test.Coverage {
429: 			mapped[coverageID] = append(mapped[coverageID], test.ID)
430: 		}
431: 	}
432: 	mapping.Requirements = make([]SmokeCoverageRequirement, 0, len(mapping.RequiredCoverage))
433: 	for _, coverageID := range mapping.RequiredCoverage {
434: 		tests := append([]string(nil), mapped[coverageID]...)
435: 		sort.Strings(tests)
436: 		mapping.Requirements = append(mapping.Requirements, SmokeCoverageRequirement{ID: coverageID, Description: descriptions[coverageID], MappedTests: tests})
437: 	}
438: 	mapping.EnsureMatrix()
439: }

441: func selectSmoke(d smokeDiscovery, sprint string, req SmokeRequest) (smokeSelection, error) {
442: 	levels, suites, tests := map[string]smokeLevel{}, map[string]smokeSuite{}, map[string]smokeTest{}
443: 	for _, v := range d.Levels {
444: 		levels[v.ID] = v
445: 	}
446: 	for _, v := range d.Suites {
447: 		suites[v.ID] = v
448: 	}
449: 	for _, v := range d.Tests {
450: 		tests[v.ID] = v
451: 	}
452: 	var mapping *smokeSprintMapping
453: 	for i := range d.SprintMappings {
454: 		if d.SprintMappings[i].Sprint == sprint {
455: 			if mapping != nil {
456: 				return smokeSelection{}, smokeError("smoke_mapping_duplicate", "scope", "multiple sprint mappings are ambiguous", "Keep one deterministic sprint mapping.", nil)
457: 			}
458: 			mapping = &d.SprintMappings[i]
459: 		}
460: 	}
461: 	if mapping != nil && mapping.NotApplicable {
462: 		return smokeSelection{Verdict: SmokeNotApplicable, Rationale: mapping.Rationale, NextAction: "No smoke action is required for this sprint."}, nil
463: 	}
464: 	checkPrereqs := func(ids []string) ([]string, bool) {
465: 		var missing []string
466: 		for _, id := range ids {
467: 			found := false
468: 			for _, p := range d.Prerequisites {
469: 				if p.ID == id {
470: 					found = true
471: 					if p.Status != "available" {
472: 						missing = append(missing, firstNonEmptyString(p.Description, p.ID)+firstSuffix(p.Action, "; action: "))
473: 					}
474: 				}
475: 			}
476: 			if !found {
477: 				missing = append(missing, id+"; action: fix the discovery prerequisite relationship")
478: 			}
479: 		}
480: 		return missing, len(missing) == 0
481: 	}
482: 	if req.Level != "" {
483: 		level, ok := levels[req.Level]
484: 		if !ok {
485: 			return smokeSelection{}, smokeError("smoke_scope_unknown", "scope", "unknown level "+req.Level, "Choose a discovered level.", nil)
486: 		}
487: 		var prereqs []string
488: 		for _, id := range level.Suites {
489: 			prereqs = append(prereqs, suites[id].Prerequisites...)
490: 		}
491: 		missing, ok := checkPrereqs(prereqs)
492: 		if !ok {
493: 			return smokeSelection{Verdict: SmokeBlockedVerdict, Prerequisites: missing, NextAction: "Satisfy the listed prerequisites and rerun smoke."}, nil
494: 		}
495: 		complete := mapping != nil && mapping.Complete && len(mapping.RequiredCoverage) > 0 && containsAll(level.Suites, mapping.Suites)
496: 		return smokeSelection{Kind: "level", IDs: []string{level.ID}, Rationale: "explicit level override", DiagnosticOnly: !complete, DurationClass: level.DurationClass, CostClass: level.CostClass}, nil
497: 	}
498: 	if req.Suite != "" {
499: 		suite, ok := suites[req.Suite]
500: 		if !ok {
501: 			return smokeSelection{}, smokeError("smoke_scope_unknown", "scope", "unknown suite "+req.Suite, "Choose a discovered suite.", nil)
502: 		}
503: 		missing, ok := checkPrereqs(suite.Prerequisites)
504: 		if !ok {
505: 			return smokeSelection{Verdict: SmokeBlockedVerdict, Prerequisites: missing, NextAction: "Satisfy the listed prerequisites and rerun smoke."}, nil
506: 		}
507: 		complete := mapping != nil && mapping.Complete && len(mapping.RequiredCoverage) > 0 && len(mapping.Suites) == 1 && mapping.Suites[0] == suite.ID
508: 		return smokeSelection{Kind: "suite", IDs: []string{suite.ID}, Rationale: "explicit suite override", DiagnosticOnly: !complete, DurationClass: suite.DurationClass, CostClass: suite.CostClass}, nil
509: 	}
510: 	if req.Test != "" {
511: 		test, ok := tests[req.Test]
512: 		if !ok {
513: 			return smokeSelection{}, smokeError("smoke_scope_unknown", "scope", "unknown test "+req.Test, "Choose a discovered test.", nil)
514: 		}
515: 		suite := suites[test.Suite]
516: 		missing, ok := checkPrereqs(suite.Prerequisites)
517: 		if !ok {
518: 			return smokeSelection{Verdict: SmokeBlockedVerdict, Prerequisites: missing, NextAction: "Satisfy the listed prerequisites and rerun smoke."}, nil
519: 		}
520: 		return smokeSelection{Kind: "test", IDs: []string{test.ID}, Rationale: "explicit diagnostic test override", DiagnosticOnly: true, DurationClass: suite.DurationClass, CostClass: suite.CostClass}, nil
521: 	}
522: 	if mapping == nil || !mapping.Complete || len(mapping.Suites) == 0 || len(mapping.RequiredCoverage) == 0 {
523: 		return smokeSelection{Verdict: SmokeBlockedVerdict, Rationale: "discovery cannot prove enumerated deep-smoke coverage for this sprint", NextAction: "Update the harness with required coverage IDs and non-empty sprint-specific tests, then rerun smoke."}, nil
524: 	}
525: 	ids := append([]string(nil), mapping.Suites...)
526: 	sort.Strings(ids)
527: 	var prereqs []string
528: 	for _, id := range ids {
529: 		suite, ok := suites[id]
530: 		if !ok {
531: 			return smokeSelection{}, smokeError("smoke_mapping_unknown", "scope", "mapping references unknown suite "+id, "Fix discovery mappings.", nil)
532: 		}
533: 		prereqs = append(prereqs, suite.Prerequisites...)
534: 	}
535: 	missing, ok := checkPrereqs(prereqs)
536: 	if !ok {
537: 		return smokeSelection{Verdict: SmokeBlockedVerdict, Prerequisites: missing, Rationale: mapping.Rationale, NextAction: "Satisfy the listed prerequisites and rerun smoke."}, nil
538: 	}
539: 	return smokeSelection{Kind: "suite", IDs: ids, Rationale: firstNonEmptyString(mapping.Rationale, "narrowest complete sprint mapping")}, nil
540: }

542: func protocolMajor(value string) int {
543: 	first := strings.SplitN(value, ".", 2)[0]
544: 	n, _ := strconv.Atoi(first)
545: 	return n
546: }
547: func contains(values []string, wanted string) bool {
548: 	for _, v := range values {
549: 		if v == wanted {
550: 			return true
551: 		}
552: 	}
553: 	return false
554: }
555: func containsAll(values, wanted []string) bool {
556: 	for _, value := range wanted {
557: 		if !contains(values, value) {
558: 			return false
559: 		}
560: 	}
561: 	return len(wanted) > 0
562: }
563: func validProtocolEnvName(value string) bool {
564: 	if value == "" {
565: 		return false
566: 	}
567: 	for i, r := range value {
568: 		if !(r == '_' || r >= 'A' && r <= 'Z' || i > 0 && r >= '0' && r <= '9') {
569: 			return false
570: 		}
571: 	}
572: 	return true
573: }
574: func firstSuffix(value, prefix string) string {
575: 	if strings.TrimSpace(value) == "" {
576: 		return ""
577: 	}
578: 	return prefix + value
579: }

581: func smokePathsOverlap(left, right string) bool {
582: 	left = filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Clean(left))
583: 	right = filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Clean(right))

291: func validateSmokeStageState(root string, sp Sprint, state SmokeStageState, path string) error {
292: 	switch state.Status {
293: 	case SmokeReady, SmokeRunning, SmokeCompleted, SmokeFailed, SmokeCancelled:
294: 	default:
295: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: smoke has unsupported status %q", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path, state.Status)
296: 	}
297: 	if state.Verdict != "" && !validSmokeVerdict(state.Verdict) {
298: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: smoke has unsupported verdict %q", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path, state.Verdict)
299: 	}
300: 	if state.Path != ArtifactRelPath(sp, StageSmoke) {
301: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: smoke path mismatch", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path)
302: 	}
303: 	if _, err := resolveSprintContained(root, sp, state.Path); err != nil {
304: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: unsafe smoke path: %v", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path, err)
305: 	}
306: 	for _, d := range state.Diagnostics {
307: 		if len(d) > 240 {
308: 			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: smoke diagnostic too long", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path)
309: 		}
310: 	}
311: 	if err := validateAttempt(state.ActiveAttempt, true); err != nil {
312: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: smoke active attempt: %v", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path, err)
313: 	}
314: 	if err := validateAttempt(state.LastAttempt, false); err != nil {
315: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: smoke last attempt: %v", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path, err)
316: 	}
317: 	if state.Override != nil {
318: 		if !state.Override.Requested || !state.Override.Confirmed || strings.TrimSpace(state.Override.Rationale) == "" || len(state.Override.Rationale) > 240 || strings.ContainsAny(state.Override.Rationale, "\x00\r\n") {
319: 			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: invalid diagnostic override", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path)
320: 		}
321: 	}
322: 	for _, issue := range state.Issues {
323: 		if issue.ID == "" || (issue.Status != "open" && issue.Status != "resolved") {
324: 			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: invalid smoke issue", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path)
325: 		}
326: 	}
327: 	if state.LastComplete != nil {
328: 		if state.LastComplete.Artifact != ArtifactRelPath(sp, StageSmoke) || state.LastComplete.CompletedAt.IsZero() || state.LastComplete.InputFingerprint == "" || state.LastComplete.ArtifactDigest == "" {
329: 			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: invalid smoke lastComplete", ErrFlowStateMalformed, path)
330: 		}
331: 	}

19: const stageSessionSchemaVersion = 1
20: 
21: type stageSessionRecord struct {
22: 	SessionID      string    `json:"sessionId"`
23: 	Provider       string    `json:"provider,omitempty"`
24: 	Model          string    `json:"model,omitempty"`
25: 	WorkDir        string    `json:"workDir"`
26: 	PromptChecksum string    `json:"promptChecksum,omitempty"`
27: 	UpdatedAt      time.Time `json:"updatedAt"`
28: }
29: 
30: type stageSessionState struct {
31: 	SchemaVersion int                           `json:"schemaVersion"`
32: 	Sessions      map[string]stageSessionRecord `json:"sessions"`
33: }
34: 
35: func stageSessionPath(sp Sprint) string { return filepath.Join(sp.Path, ".stage-sessions.json") }
36: 
37: func loadStageSessions(sp Sprint) (stageSessionState, error) {
38: 	path := stageSessionPath(sp)
39: 	data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
40: 	if errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
41: 		return stageSessionState{SchemaVersion: stageSessionSchemaVersion, Sessions: map[string]stageSessionRecord{}}, nil
42: 	}
43: 	if err != nil {
44: 		return stageSessionState{}, err
45: 	}
46: 	var state stageSessionState
47: 	dec := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(data))
48: 	dec.DisallowUnknownFields()
49: 	if err := dec.Decode(&state); err != nil {
50: 		return stageSessionState{}, fmt.Errorf("decode stage sessions: %w", err)
51: 	}
52: 	var trailing any
53: 	if err := dec.Decode(&trailing); !errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
54: 		return stageSessionState{}, fmt.Errorf("decode stage sessions: trailing JSON")
55: 	}
56: 	if state.SchemaVersion != stageSessionSchemaVersion || state.Sessions == nil {
57: 		return stageSessionState{}, fmt.Errorf("unsupported stage session state")
58: 	}
59: 	return state, nil
60: }
61: 
62: func saveStageSessions(sp Sprint, state stageSessionState) error {
63: 	data, err := json.MarshalIndent(state, "", "  ")
64: 	if err != nil {
65: 		return err
66: 	}
67: 	data = append(data, '\n')
68: 	path := stageSessionPath(sp)
69: 	tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(sp.Path, ".stage-sessions.*.tmp")
70: 	if err != nil {
71: 		return err
72: 	}
73: 	tmpPath := tmp.Name()
74: 	defer os.Remove(tmpPath)
75: 	if _, err = tmp.Write(data); err == nil {
76: 		err = tmp.Chmod(0o600)
77: 	}
78: 	if closeErr := tmp.Close(); err == nil {
79: 		err = closeErr
80: 	}
81: 	if err != nil {
82: 		return err
83: 	}
84: 	return os.Rename(tmpPath, path)
85: }
86: 
87: func stageSessionCompatible(record stageSessionRecord, req pruntime.Request) bool {
88: 	// Prompt checksums are retained for diagnostics only. Exact prompt matching
89: 	// would make interrupted-session recovery brittle after harmless artifact
90: 	// edits; the continuation explicitly tells the agent to reread current state.
91: 	return record.SessionID != "" && record.Provider == req.Provider && record.Model == req.Model && record.WorkDir == req.WorkDir
92: }
93: 
94: func stageSessionKey(stage PlanningStage, req pruntime.Request) string {
95: 	parts := []string{string(stage)}
96: 	for _, dimension := range []string{"task", "coverage", "area"} {
97: 		parts = append(parts, strings.TrimSpace(req.Metadata[dimension]))
98: 	}
99: 	if parts[1] == "" && parts[2] == "" && parts[3] == "" {
100: 		return parts[0]
101: 	}
102: 	return strings.Join(parts, ":")
103: }
104: 
105: func (s Service) startPlanningStageRun(ctx context.Context, sp Sprint, stage PlanningStage, req pruntime.Request) (pruntime.Result, error) {
106: 	key := stageSessionKey(stage, req)
107: 	originalPrompt := req.Prompt
108: 	continuing := false
109: 	state, loadErr := loadStageSessions(sp)
110: 	if loadErr == nil {
111: 		if record, ok := state.Sessions[key]; ok && stageSessionCompatible(record, req) {
112: 			req.SessionID = record.SessionID
113: 			req.SessionAction = "continue"
114: 			req.Prompt = insertStageContinuation(req.Prompt, "Continue the interrupted UltraPlan stage from the existing session. Re-read the current stage prompt and filesystem state, then finish only the requested stage.")
115: 			continuing = true
116: 		}
117: 	}
118: 	previousOnEvent := req.OnEvent
119: 	var mu sync.Mutex
120: 	lastSession := req.SessionID
121: 	persist := func(sessionID string) {
122: 		if strings.TrimSpace(sessionID) == "" {
123: 			return
124: 		}
125: 		mu.Lock()
126: 		defer mu.Unlock()
127: 		if sessionID == lastSession {
128: 			return
129: 		}
130: 		lastSession = sessionID
131: 		current, err := loadStageSessions(sp)
132: 		if err != nil {
133: 			return
134: 		}
135: 		current.Sessions[key] = stageSessionRecord{SessionID: sessionID, Provider: req.Provider, Model: req.Model, WorkDir: req.WorkDir, PromptChecksum: req.PromptRef.Checksum, UpdatedAt: s.now().UTC()}
136: 		_ = saveStageSessions(sp, current)
137: 	}
138: 	req.OnEvent = func(event pruntime.Event) {
139: 		if previousOnEvent != nil {
140: 			previousOnEvent(event)
141: 		}
142: 		persist(event.SessionID)
143: 	}
144: 	result, err := s.startSprintRuntime(ctx, sp, stage, req)
145: 	persist(result.SessionID)
146: 	if continuing && planningSessionNotFound(result, err) && ctx.Err() == nil {
147: 		_ = clearPlanningStageSessionKey(sp, key)
148: 		lastSession = ""
149: 		req.SessionID = ""
150: 		req.SessionAction = "fresh"
151: 		req.Prompt = originalPrompt
152: 		result, err = s.startSprintRuntime(ctx, sp, stage, req)
153: 		persist(result.SessionID)
154: 	}
155: 	return result, err
156: }
157: 
158: func planningSessionNotFound(result pruntime.Result, err error) bool {
159: 	var details []string
160: 	if err != nil {
161: 		details = append(details, err.Error())
162: 	}
163: 	details = append(details, result.TerminalOutput)
164: 	if result.Error != nil {
165: 		details = append(details, result.Error.UserDetail, result.Error.DebugDetail)
166: 	}
167: 	for _, attempt := range result.Attempts {
168: 		details = append(details, attempt.ErrorDetail)
169: 	}
170: 	return strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(strings.Join(details, "\n")), "session not found")
171: }
172: 
173: func insertStageContinuation(prompt, instruction string) string {
174: 	boundary := strings.Index(prompt, sharedPromptStageBoundary)
175: 	if boundary < 0 {
176: 		return instruction + "\n\n" + prompt
177: 	}
178: 	boundary += len(sharedPromptStageBoundary)
179: 	return prompt[:boundary] + instruction + "\n\n" + prompt[boundary:]
180: }
181: 
182: func clearPlanningStageSession(sp Sprint, stage PlanningStage) error {
183: 	state, err := loadStageSessions(sp)
184: 	if err != nil {
185: 		return err
186: 	}
187: 	found := false
188: 	for key := range state.Sessions {
189: 		if key == string(stage) || strings.HasPrefix(key, string(stage)+":") {
190: 			delete(state.Sessions, key)
191: 			found = true
192: 		}
193: 	}
194: 	if !found {
195: 		return nil
196: 	}
197: 	return saveOrRemoveStageSessions(sp, state)
198: }
199: 
200: func clearPlanningStageSessionKey(sp Sprint, key string) error {
201: 	state, err := loadStageSessions(sp)
202: 	if err != nil {
203: 		return err
204: 	}
205: 	if _, ok := state.Sessions[key]; !ok {
206: 		return nil
207: 	}
208: 	delete(state.Sessions, key)
209: 	return saveOrRemoveStageSessions(sp, state)
210: }
211: 
212: func saveOrRemoveStageSessions(sp Sprint, state stageSessionState) error {
213: 	if len(state.Sessions) == 0 {
214: 		if err := os.Remove(stageSessionPath(sp)); err != nil && !errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
215: 			return err
216: 		}
217: 		return nil
218: 	}
219: 	return saveStageSessions(sp, state)
220: }
221: 
222: func (s Service) cleanupPlanningStageSession(ctx context.Context, sp Sprint, stage PlanningStage, sessionID string) error {
223: 	if err := s.deleteCompletedSession(ctx, sessionID); err != nil {
224: 		return err
225: 	}
226: 	return clearPlanningStageSession(sp, stage)
227: }
228: 
229: func (s Service) cleanupPlanningStageSessions(ctx context.Context, sp Sprint, stage PlanningStage, result pruntime.Result) error {
230: 	if err := s.deleteCompletedSessions(ctx, result); err != nil {
231: 		return err
232: 	}
233: 	return clearPlanningStageSession(sp, stage)
234: }

39: 	r.calls = append(r.calls, append([]string{req.Executable}, req.Args...))
40: 	result := pprocess.Result{ExitCode: 0, CleanupComplete: true, StartedAt: time.Now(), FinishedAt: time.Now()}
41: 	if r.malformed {
42: 		result.Stdout = "not-json"
43: 		return result, nil
44: 	}
45: 	var value any = r.run
46: 	for _, arg := range req.Args {
47: 		if arg == "discover" {
48: 			value = r.discovery
49: 		}
50: 	}
51: 	data, _ := json.Marshal(value)
52: 	result.Stdout = string(data)
53: 	return result, nil
54: }

10:This TRD defines the technical requirements for UltraPlan Go, a production-grade local CLI, TUI, and browser surface that implement the proven UltraPlan workflow. Phase 1 covers study initialization, source analysis, report synthesis, code-reference extraction, resumable orchestration, validation, and operational diagnostics. Phase 2 adds governed project and sprint planning through `plan.md`, then controlled implementation execution through `execute`. Phase 5 begins with Sprint 33 and inserts a validated `code-context` stage after requirements, then reuses its exact Markdown source pack through downstream agent-backed stages. Phase 6 begins with Sprint 35 and establishes durable workspace-wide run identity, lifecycle/liveness projection, replayable sanitized events, cross-surface control, and correlated operational telemetry.

### 18.9 Phase 3 Review And Deep Smoke Requirements

#### 18.9.1 Review Scope And Execution

Review preflight must:

- require valid governed inputs through `execute`
- resolve every selected contract and review protocol from `project-index.md`
- reject missing, duplicate, unknown, unreadable, or escaping catalog paths
- compute a deterministic fingerprint over requirements, sprint index, technical handbook, area reasoning, final reasoning, plan, execute state/summary, selected contracts/protocols, target implementation identity, and explicit changed-path scope
- show the selected model source, reviewer count, concurrency, target scope, and permitted writes in dry-run/TUI confirmation

UltraPlan, not the model, owns reviewer fan-out. It must issue one independent structured agentwrap request per selected contract plus one handbook request, with bounded concurrency, context cancellation, read-only permissions, and validated JSON results. A reviewer must classify each requirement/guidance item as direct, partial, not triggered, or explicitly deferred before judging conformance.

Deterministic product checks must cover decision conformance, plan-task execution evidence, approved verification-command results, citation containment/line validity, complete reviewer coverage, deviations, and missing evidence. Runtime exit success alone cannot produce a passing review.

The final review verdict is computed by product code. The final Markdown is written atomically to the sprint-root `review.md`, replacing the prior manual or generated file only when the command has permission to run. A failed/incomplete new review must not corrupt the last complete review artifact; current failed state and diagnostics remain visible through flow state and status.

#### 18.9.2 Smoke Harness Contract And Execution

`project-index.md` must catalog the smoke harness root and versioned manifest. The manifest must describe an executable plus argument prefix, protocol version, machine-readable discovery/run commands, bounded authoring paths, evidence directories, and supported capability flags. UltraPlan must never execute a shell command parsed from Markdown or README prose.

Before discovery on every non-dry smoke run, UltraPlan must invoke the configured smoke author model in the external harness. The author receives the governed sprint inputs, execute/review evidence, target implementation, deterministic test inventory, existing harness, and manifest-declared writable paths. It must create or update a durable sprint-specific suite for real boundaries that deterministic unit/integration tests cannot prove. Those boundaries include real provider/model behavior where the product path uses a provider, process and signal lifecycle, real filesystem/configuration, network, credentials, browser engines, timing, cancellation, and platform behavior. It must not duplicate ordinary deterministic verification or introduce a provider call into an otherwise offline product path.

Harness discovery must return structured levels, suites, enumerated tests, per-test coverage IDs, sprint mappings with required coverage IDs, runtime/network/credential prerequisites, expected duration/cost class, and evidence schema version. A complete mapping with empty suites, empty tests, missing required coverage, or unassigned coverage must not pass. Smoke selection prefers the authored sprint-specific suite, then directly mapped suites, then explicit tests for investigation. A narrow passing rerun does not replace required evidence from its containing suite.

Smoke execution must:

- require a current passing or non-blocking review by default
- record the smoke author run/model and every changed harness path
- show scope, prerequisites, model/runtime, duration/cost class, allowed mutation roots, and external evidence destination before execution
- use explicit argv, contained cwd, bounded environment forwarding, timeout, context cancellation, and descendant-process cleanup
- validate the harness run ID, exit/result counts, evidence paths, evidence identity, and relevant open/resolved issue references
- keep raw run JSON, stdout/stderr, per-test artifacts, and issue files in the harness
- atomically write the linked human-readable sprint-root `smoke.md` after validating the authoring scope and enumerated executed test identities
- classify unavailable required environment as blocked and irrelevant scope as not applicable

The product review/smoke workflows must not edit product source, product tests, governed sprint inputs, or Git state. Smoke authoring may edit only manifest-declared harness authoring paths; run and issue evidence remains confined to the manifest-declared evidence roots. Any other harness change or any product/governed-input identity change fails smoke.

#### 18.9.3 Flow, Freshness, And TUI Parity

The default order is `execute -> review -> smoke`. Blocking/high review findings stop smoke unless an explicit diagnostic override is confirmed. Flow state records execution status, verdict, artifact path, timestamp, input fingerprint, run/evidence ID where applicable, and safe diagnostics for both stages.

Any governed input, selected contract/protocol, execute evidence, or implementation fingerprint change makes the prior review stale. A stale review also makes smoke stale. Status, JSON, and TUI must agree on readiness, running/completed/failed/cancelled state, verdict, staleness, artifact, evidence link, and required next action.

Every Phase 3 delivery sprint must update the TUI in the same sprint. TUI operations use the shared app use cases and expose the same review/smoke scope, dry-run, confirmation, progress, cancellation, results, focused reruns, evidence links, and recovery behavior as the CLI. TUI code must not invoke CLI handlers, parse terminal output, interpret native provider payloads, or persist an alternate verification state.

Normal tests use fake review runtimes and a fake smoke harness. Required tests cover success, findings, blocking failure, missing reviewer result, malformed structured output, stale inputs, missing harness, missing coverage, blocked environment, not-applicable scope, timeout, cancellation, malformed harness output, missing evidence, path escape, redaction, CLI/JSON/TUI agreement, and recovery.

### 18.10 Deferred Technical Requirements

The following remain explicitly deferred:

- general-purpose issue tracking and remote issue synchronization
- automatic product/test fixes from findings
- Git add/commit/push
- cross-sprint review/smoke scheduler
- hosted review or smoke service

## 18A. Phase 4 Local Web Surface Technical Requirements

Phase 4 is an interface expansion, not a new product workflow. `internal/web` owns HTTP routing, transport validation, HTML/template rendering, embedded static assets, browser-session protection, and SSE connections. It must not own study/project/sprint state machines, prompt construction, runtime or smoke invocation, verdict computation, artifact persistence, durable run identity, or durable recovery.

The required dependency direction is:

```text
cmd/ultraplan -> internal/app + internal/tui + internal/web
internal/web  -> internal/app
internal/web  -> no product modules directly
internal/app  -> product modules + platform modules
```

Interface runners and other side-effectful surface dependencies should be constructed explicitly at the composition root and passed inward. Phase 4 must not add another package-global mutable runner registration.

Required initial route capabilities:

```text
GET    /                         browser dashboard
GET    /projects/...             browser project and sprint pages
GET    /studies/...              browser study pages
GET    /api/v1/dashboard         structured dashboard state
GET    /api/v1/artifacts/{ref}   bounded allowlisted preview
POST   /api/v1/validations       read-only validation
POST   /api/v1/operations/prepare guarded-operation confirmation
POST   /api/v1/operations        start confirmed operation
GET    /api/v1/operations/{id}   compatibility projection to stable run status/result
GET    /api/v1/operations/{id}/events compatibility projection to replayable progress
DELETE /api/v1/operations/{id}   compatibility cancellation request
GET    /api/v1/runs              workspace-wide durable run projection
GET    /api/v1/runs/{id}         durable run status/result/recovery
GET    /api/v1/runs/{id}/events  cursor-based replay and live progress
DELETE /api/v1/runs/{id}         authorized idempotent cancellation request
```

Exact resource detail routes may evolve, but `/api/v1` JSON and error envelopes are compatibility-controlled once documented. Unknown `/api/` routes return structured JSON errors and must never fall through to an HTML page.

The server delivery hub is ephemeral and bounded. It may hold normalized requests, current connections, and delivery buffers, but not the only run IDs, cancellation routes, history, or terminal results. Server restart recovery reads the durable run projection and package-owned product state. Slow or disconnected SSE subscribers must not block product execution. Compatibility operation URLs must resolve to the durable run, a retained tombstone, or a typed recovery response; session expiry or in-memory reaping alone cannot produce an unexplained 404 for a valid run.

part.text: One more precise look at the CLI arg parsing for smoke.

reasoning_details.text:
I have everything I need. Let me also do one final sanity check on a couple of details I want to state precisely:

1. In `runSmoke`, the discovery args: `manifest.Args + manifest.Commands.Discover + ["--target", prepared.Target]`. Run args: `manifest.Args + Commands.Run + ["--project", ..., "--sprint", ..., "--workspace", s.root, "--target", prepared.Target, "--scope-kind", selection.Kind, "--scope", strings.Join(selection.IDs, ",")]`.

2. `smokeEnvironment`: names = settings.Environment ∪ (manifest.Environment ∩ allowed(settings.Environment))... wait: `for _, name := range manifest.Environment { if allowed[name] && !contains(names, name) { names = append(names, name) } }`. So the manifest can only request env names already in settings.Environment (the config allowlist). So effective allowlist = settings.Environment; manifest.Environment is an intersection filter that adds nothing new. Interesting descriptive fact: the manifest's environment list cannot expand the allowlist; it only permits names already allowlisted by configuration. Both must agree for forwarding. Values come from getenv; empty values dropped.

3. Timeout selection: req.Timeout > 0 → "request"; else if Sources["smoke.run_timeout"] ∈ {workspace, env} → settings.RunTimeout with source; else manifest.Defaults.Timeout valid → "manifest"; else settings.RunTimeout with source label or "default".

4. Note in RunSmoke: after successful commit and roadmap reconciliation, publication re-runs prepareSmokeStatic. If that fails, error joined with err (which is nil) → returns non-nil error even though smoke completed and committed. Describe as-is.

5. Diagnostic-only results return WITHOUT committing (line 180-182: `if result.DiagnosticOnly { return result, nil }`) — so diagnostic runs don't write smoke.md or flow-state LastComplete... but wait — saveSmokeAttempt(terminal) was still called by RunSmoke wrapper at line 35 (after runSmoke returns). Yes: RunSmoke always calls saveSmokeAttempt terminal. So flow-state Smoke.LastAttempt records the failed/diagnostic attempt but no artifact commit. Also note: for blocked/not-applicable selections (verdict blocked/not_applicable), commitSmoke IS invoked (line 129-135) unless DryRun — those write smoke.md with verdict blocked/not_applicable. DiagnosticOnly test/level/suite overrides with actual run results return without commit (line 180-182).

Hmm wait, careful reading of lines 128-135:
```go
result.DiagnosticOnly = selection.DiagnosticOnly || (req.ForceReview && (review fail/blocked))
if selection.Verdict == SmokeBlockedVerdict || selection.Verdict == SmokeNotApplicable {
    result.Status, result.Verdict, result.NextAction = SmokeCompleted, selection.Verdict, ...
    if req.DryRun { return result, nil }
    return s.commitSmoke(prepared, result)
}
```
So blocked/N.A. are committed as completed-with-verdict. And ForceReview with fail/blocked review sets DiagnosticOnly=true — then if selection verdict is normal (suites selected), the harness RUNS, evidence validated, verdict synthesized, then line 180: `if result.DiagnosticOnly { return result, nil }` — no commit. Good.

Also note line 136-139: selection.DiagnosticOnly appends diagnostics + NextAction about containing suite.

6. Roadmap reconciliation condition includes ReviewVerdict pass/pass_with_findings AND verdict pass AND !DiagnosticOnly. Publication workspace paths include roadmap.md only when verdict pass && !diagnostic. So both fire together except review-verdict nuance (roadmap marking additionally requires acceptable review verdict). Fine.

7. `RenderSmoke` uses `time.Now().UTC()` directly (not s.now()).

8. ValidateSmokeContent forbidden content: "-----BEGIN", "Authorization: Bearer", `"stdout":`, `"stderr":`.

9. smokeIdentityReferences includes manifest path file digest + review.md digest + facts + evidence files + issue files. Sorted by path then kind. refreshEvidenceFingerprint re-hashes files at call time.

10. The `.runtime-metrics.json` record for smoke authoring: stage=smoke, operation=author.

11. Trust boundaries:
   - Harness stdout decoded via decodeOneJSON → discovery/response become verification truth.
   - Manifest JSON from harness tree (cataloged in project-index.md — user-authored markdown) → executable argv/env/cwd.
   - Env allowlist intersection.
   - Author agent output → harness tree changes within declared paths (snapshot diff enforced).
   - Evidence paths from response resolved inside RunsRoot/IssuesRoot.

The product does not own smoke tests; it owns the *gate* around them: 1. **Static readiness** (`prepareSmokeStatic`): exactly one `Smoke Harnesses` catalog row in `project-index.md`, a valid target implementation directory, a manifest-contained executable/cwd/evidence roots, and a current, non-stale, acceptable Conformance Review (fail/blocked reviews admit only a confirmed diagnostic override). 2. **Agent-driven authoring** inside the harness: one restricted-permission agent call may modify only manifest-declared authoring paths; the whole harness tree is hashed before/after and any out-of-allowlist change fails the run. 3. **Machine-readable discovery** executed as a direct bounded child process; its JSON is validated for identity, referential closure, and coverage assignment. 4. **Scope selection**: narrowest sufficient scope (explicit level/suite/test override or the authored complete sprint mapping); narrower-than-containing scopes and forced-review runs are marked `DiagnosticOnly` and never commit evidence. 5. **Direct argv execution** of the harness `run` command with env allowlist, timeouts, output caps, and process-group cleanup — the only non-agentwrap subprocess lane in this surface. 6. **Evidence validation**: run identity, scope echo, count arithmetic, exact executed-test-set equality vs discovery, evidence/issue path containment plus optional hashes, failed-test⇒open-issue completeness. 7. **Atomic publication**: `ValidateSmokeContent`-clean `smoke.md` written atomically, then full `SmokeStageState` (+ `LastComplete`) committed to flow-state, then optional roadmap delivery mark, then git publication — strictly in that order. ## 2. Invariants (as implemented) - No harness work starts unless: exactly-one catalog row, contained manifest/executable/cwd/roots, valid protocol-v1 manifest, and a current acceptable (or explicitly overridden) review. - Authoring changes outside the declared path set reject the entire run; symlinks and oversized/unbounded harness trees abort snapshotting. - Discovery and run responses must be exactly one JSON value each; truncated streams are failures, not data loss. - Executed tests must equal discovered selected tests exactly (set + counts); every failure needs an open, fully-populated, ID-addressed issue under the issues root. - Diagnostic-only outcomes never write smoke.md or flow-state verification evidence (but their attempts are recorded in flow state via the wrapper). - Canonical smoke.md changes only via fsync+rename of a fully validated render; malformed/failed reruns preserve the previous artifact (test-pinned). - Flow-state commit happens after artifact commit; roadmap mark after flow-state commit; git publication last; every later failure leaves earlier artifacts intact and reports reconciliation guidance instead of rolling back. - Raw harness streams/secrets never enter smoke.md (validator forbidden-substring list; SafeArgv redaction; env values never persisted). - Blocked/not-applicable are *completed* verdicts (committed), distinct from execution failure. ## 11. Trust boundaries - Harness stdout is decoded and **executed as verification truth** (discovery graph steers selection/expected-test sets; run response decides verdict inputs) — mitigations: identity quadruples, referential closure validation, arithmetic checks, exact test-set equality, evidence containment + hashing, exit-code coherence. - Manifest (JSON in the harness tree) selects the executable/argv prefix/cwd/evidence roots/authoring allowlist/env names — mitigations: cataloged absolute root, EvalSymlinks+containment on every path, capability/schema gates, env-name grammar, overlap rejection. The catalog row itself comes from user-authored project-index.md markdown (never executed as commands). - Manifest-declared env names cross the allowlist boundary: effective names = config allowlist ∩ manifest list (manifest cannot expand), values sourced at spawn time. - The authoring agent receives governed inputs verbatim (direct-input packet) and works inside the harness with restricted permissions; enforcement relies on runtime permission support (`UnsupportedCount` gate) plus the unconditional post-hoc tree diff. - This is the product's direct non-agentwrap argv execution lane (per canonical surface map; QA's approved-check lane lives in a different surface). Child output is bounded and truncated streams are rejected rather than parsed. - smoke.md renders selected harness-controlled strings (IDs, titles, summaries) through `printable()` (backtick flattening) and the forbidden-content validator; diagnostics persist through `safeError` sanitization. ## 12. Cancellation / retry / restart / error semantics - Cancellation: ctx propagates into both child processes (group SIGTERM→SIGKILL with grace; CleanupComplete false if pgid lookup fails ⇒ `smoke_cleanup`) and is checked after authoring (`smoke_author_cancelled`); `smokeAttemptStatus` maps context.Canceled/SmokeCancelled ⇒ AttemptCancelled. Durable CLI acceptance provides the cancellable ctx; web/TUI cancel flows through the operation hub (other surface). - Timeout: discovery and run have independent timeouts; timeout classification distinguishes `smoke_timeout` from generic process failure; request/config/manifest provenance recorded. - Retry/rerun: rerunning smoke repeats the full pipeline; successful reruns atomically replace smoke.md and the Smoke record; failed reruns preserve the prior artifact AND restore Verdict/RunID/EvidenceID from LastComplete in flow state. Authoring resumes prior sessions when provider/model/workdir match, with one fresh-session fallback. - Restart/crash: a crash between artifact write and flow-state save leaves smoke.md updated with `Reconciliation=true` guidance on next observation; a crash mid-attempt leaves a running attempt record that flow-state-surface reconcile (`attemptExpired`: dead PID immediate, else 2h heartbeat window — heartbeated once at attempt start here) converts to timed_out/interrupted. No cleanup-uncertain marker is produced by this surface. - Error envelope: every failure path funnels through `smokeFailedResult` + typed `SmokeError` (code/category/message/guidance/wrapped cause); CLI maps categories to exit classes; JSON consumers get the full typed result. ## 13. atomic smoke.md after validating authoring scope and enumerated identities; unavailable required env ⇒ blocked; irrelevant scope ⇒ not applicable). - ~L2070: product review/smoke workflows must not edit product source/tests/governed inputs/Git; flow state records execution status vs verdict distinction, input fingerprints; stale review makes smoke stale; CLI/TUI agreement. - ~L1953-1959: smoke.md validator requirements (exists post-completion, no placeholders, identifies project/sprint/review verdict+fingerprint/harness/scope/rationale/environment/model/date, five-verdict enum). - ~L50-55: non-goals — no auto-fixes, no Git mutation during smoke, harness owns detailed run/issue persistence. - ARCHITECTURE.md: L32/146 smoke.go responsibility split;
